title: Record
description:
A stream starts with exactly one manifest. All remaining values are
independently staged and validated before the receiving archive writes.

AcceptedEncoding.description:
Original encoding retained when a numbered conversion can represent the
same accepted action and effects in the current typed prepared request.

live.description: The adapter marks queries over live state, independently of `for`.

horizon.description:
A point in time as a source stated it. Unknown times are `None` at the
use site, never a zero or a guess.

value.description:
Authored fields only. Identity and authorship are supplied by the product's
write path; `deny_unknown_fields` prevents a client forging daemon metadata.

oneOf.description: Minute of the local civil day. Calendar resolution belongs to DaySetting.
Elapsed duration, for example 20m or1.5s, in whole milliseconds
Elapsed duration, for example 20m or1.5s, in whole milliseconds

value.description: List prices in USD per million tokens.

cache_write_1h.description:
Cache writes with a one-hour lifetime, where the vendor prices them
apart from the default writes.

long.description: Rates for a response whose prompt is longer than `above` tokens.

above.description: Prompt tokens (every kind of input together) above which these apply.

tiers.description:
Multipliers for service tiers other than the standard one, by the
name the tool records (`fast`, `flex`, `priority`, ...). A tier the
model has no multiplier for leaves the cost unknown.

AssertionRecord.description:
An independently restored historical fact need not have an original native
request. Import claims do not certify native authorship or grant privilege.

blob.description: The bytes, when they were inline or found on disk and stored.

source_id.description:
The source's own ID for the file (ChatGPT `file-…`), by which an
export's separately stored bytes are found.

AttachmentBinding.description:
One attachment slot in the complete source message. Sparse projections keep
the original block ordinal instead of renumbering the blocks they carry.

candidates.description: No candidates means unknown bytes. Multiple candidates remain ambiguous.

exported_from.description:
Actual context of this export. A receiver retains it as a declaration,
independently of its own validated receiving members.

namespace.description:
Retained even when candidate bytes are unknown. Several namespaces may
describe the same source slot without merging their claims.

prior_exports.description:
Supplied prior export declarations, preserved in their original order.
Export never manufactures or appends a context history.

AttachmentCandidate.description:
A complete content hash can span several stored extents. Original source
claims remain distinct even when candidate hashes happen to agree.

AttachmentDirection.description: Whether the attachment went to the model or came from it.

oneOf.description: The source records the media without establishing model delivery or authorship.

AttachmentNamespace.description:
Original import namespace qualified by its actual source input and chain.
This is portable provenance, not receiving-archive membership authority.

AttachmentSourceClaim.description:
Historical provenance supplied by the exporting archive. These fields never
grant access to a receiving archive's inputs, chains, or import namespaces.

namespace.description:
Unknown historical provenance stays unknown; ingress never substitutes
the receiving namespace for an original source claim.

Attribution.description: Which agent, skill, plugin or MCP tool the work was done for.

AuthoredEffect.description:
A request may insert several linked records; empty effects still preserve
an entity-deduplicated request's identity and original outcome.

BackfillCounts.description: Conversations a job has handled so far.

unchanged.description: Already in the archive as the provider has them.

BackfillEvent.description: One thing that happened to a backfill job.

BackfillJob.description: A stored backfill job with everything that happened to it.

BackfillReport.description: What the extension instance holding a job reports.

position.description: Where in the provider's conversation list to continue.

Block.description: One part of a message's content, in the order the source wrote it.

signature.description:
Present when the provider sent the reasoning encrypted or
redacted; the text is then absent.

action.description:
What the call does, decided by the origin's parser from its own
tool names.

command.description: The shell command, when the call runs one.

path.description: The file the call reads or edits, when it names one.

run_by_script.description:
A command a script call ran, recorded without a call of its own:
the script's call is then not counted beside its commands.

oneOf.description:
A tool's result. It lives in the message that carried it and points
at its call by `call_id`; the call may be in an earlier message.

attachments.description: Images or files the tool returned (screenshots, rendered pages).

data.description: Structured result data the source attached beside the text.

reported_duration_ms.description: Elapsed time explicitly reported by the harness, distinct from timestamp differences.

oneOf.description: A block kind this origin's parser does not read yet. Kept whole.

CachedNativeContext.description:
The predecessor cache's partial envelope, preserved as historical metadata.
Missing full fetch fields remain absent; this is not a native observation.

ChatAction.description: A stored chat action with everything that happened to it.

ChatAttachment.description: A file attached to a chat action.

ChatEvent.description: One thing that happened to a chat action.

host.description: Present only for the standalone host deliverer. Primary uses Forward.

owner.description: The accepting machine's configured identity, within this archive.

rule_sources.description: Source revision identities for the local monotone adoption ordinal.

oneOf.description: Main-time lower bound; span-valued rows are selected by overlap.

Main-time exclusive upper bound. A date resolves to its logical-day
end, while an instant remains that instant.

ConfirmedOrigin.description:
Only owner fetch metadata supplies origin. Product payloads, names and
acquisition-route declarations cannot authenticate it.

ConservedEffects.description:
A migration's typed effect projection accompanies the original bytes. It
restores data through historical apply, never by executing the old intent.

Coverage.description:
Aggregated omission counts stay bounded by the finite target kinds/views.
Individual omitted references remain ordinary streamed Omission items.

CursorContext.description:
Context fixed on the first page. Products bind grants, schema/definition/ranking
versions and every read position here, and check their continued availability.

DaySettingWire.description:
Pure transport data. The caller resolves the named zone before constructing
a runtime setting; deserialization performs no zone database lookup.

DeliveryOutcome.description:
A durable attempt begins unknown before effects run. Persist this record in
the same owner as deliveries; only a returned receipt changes its outcome.

DeliveryOutcome2.description: What happened to a delivery after it was prepared.

oneOf.description: The product opens this reference through its ordinary read operation.

metadata.description: Source descriptors. Projected text is held only in blocks.

source_time.description: The provider's time for the source record, not an inferred writing time.

DocumentAuthorship.description: A purpose, project creator or upload does not by itself establish a writer.

oneOf.description: Elapsed duration, for example 20m or1.5s, in whole milliseconds
Refused by a permission rule, mode or the user; the source's own label.

Event.description:
A recorded fact from an input, optionally tied to a conversation.
Without a conversation, it belongs to its input and record range.

after.description: The message the event follows, when the source places it.

data.description:
Native fields kept as written, or the typed data of a normalized
observation (`observations`). A native event is used as written.

range.description:
The byte range of the record the event came from, in its input. It
places the event among the input's messages and cites its bytes.

position.description: Original order within this delivery, retained through historical restore.

ExecutionBinding.description: Complete accepted inputs retained before an execution exposes continuation calls.

accepted_request.description:
Original trusted envelope without credentials; provenance grants no authority.
Internal calls may have none. Replay uses current operation validation.

ExecutionPresentation.description: Selected source facts are read under the authenticated snapshot, not copied here.

page_budget.description: Logical limits before reserving this response's envelope bytes.

FiredIntent.description:
A firing is an intent until the host's quiet hours and attention budget have
been applied. Authorship comes from the authenticated product write path.

oneOf.description: Minute of the local civil day. Calendar resolution belongs to DaySetting.

FrozenDefinition.description: A saved definition as it was bound, including its actual syntax.

HeldRoute.description:
The owner policy that deferred this exact route. Deadlines are absolute
milliseconds; the owner resolves its current policy again after waking.

original.description: Missing historical bodies and outcomes remain unrecorded.

HistoricalAssertionEvidence.description:
A predecessor assertion remains evidence under its recorded value schema.
Its malformed or missing current fields never become a new native fact.

declared_binding_hash.description:
Optional summary claims from the original payload, distinct from the
actual fetched native record hash and projection evidence.

encoded_run.description: Exact available nested run encoding, not an acquisition-byte claim.

HistoricalRecord2.description:
Read-only restoration of recorded predecessor evidence, with no native
command or current-schema validation implied by its historical value.

HostPolicy.description:
One value belongs to the host deliverer, including all local and forwarded
product intents. Persist it atomically with emitted delivery records.

ImportAttribution.description: Computed from the local bundle ingress and authenticated importing channel.

machine.description: The receiving machine, computed by the import boundary.

ImportHistory.description: Locally observed ingress is distinct from claims carried by a bundle.

ImportedEventIdentity.description:
A stable event identity and all original claims for the selected
source reading. Equal imports union claims rather than dropping one.

InjectionEvidence.description:
Missing observed evidence means unknown injection attribution. Declared
historical claims remain available without becoming local observations.

oneOf.description:
Compatible payload fields whose original request metadata or effect
encoding cannot be represented as an unchanged current request.

LeftOut.description: A reference or section a delivery did not include, and why.

Link.description:
A relationship between two sessions, from an explicit marker in the
source, never from guessing.

at.description: The parent's message the child branched from or was spawned by.

call_id.description: The tool call in the parent that spawned the child.

evidence.description: The source field that states the link, for display and audit.

oneOf.description:
A fork: the child shares the parent's messages up to `at`, then
diverges. The child stores only its own tail.
A session spawned by a tool call in the parent (a subagent).

The same work continued in a new session (after compaction or a
resume).

The child's file repeats messages the parent originated; they are
stored once, in the parent.

Manifest.description:
The primary manifest stays small. A directory package names a streamed
inventory, rather than collecting all members in the manifest.

Message.description: One message, stored once, in the session where it originated.

attrs.description: Provider fields indexed as given, including nested citations and content details.

duration_ms.description: How long the response took, as the tool reported it.

parent.description: The message this one replies to, when the source records it.

production.description: How the harness produced the message, beyond its content.

reported_cost_usd.description: Cost the tool itself reported for this response, as written.

bindings.description: Attachment provenance is independent of the source message value and hash.

block_count.description: Original source cardinality; absent positions are unavailable or omitted.

source_version.description: Identity of the complete source value, unchanged by view projection.

NativeProjectionProvenance.description:
What the authenticated owner fetch actually supplied. Record/projection
hashes are distinct from an accepted intent hash; these fields confer no
original-capture, native-execution or importing-actor authority.

block.description:
Original Message block ordinal or canonical Document block ordinal.
This is never a text-body sequence index or local database primary key.

oneOf.description: A complete, accessible container with no text bodies; no block invented.

byte.description: UTF-8 byte offset inside the exact field or two-LF separator.

horizon.description:
A point in time as a source stated it. Unknown times are `None` at the
use site, never a zero or a guess.

value.description:
Authored fields only. Identity and authorship are supplied by the product's
write path; `deny_unknown_fields` prevents a client forging daemon metadata.

oneOf.description: Minute of the local civil day. Calendar resolution belongs to DaySetting.
Elapsed duration, for example 20m or1.5s, in whole milliseconds
Elapsed duration, for example 20m or1.5s, in whole milliseconds

value.description: List prices in USD per million tokens.

cache_write_1h.description:
Cache writes with a one-hour lifetime, where the vendor prices them
apart from the default writes.

long.description: Rates for a response whose prompt is longer than `above` tokens.

above.description: Prompt tokens (every kind of input together) above which these apply.

tiers.description:
Multipliers for service tiers other than the standard one, by the
name the tool records (`fast`, `flex`, `priority`, ...). A tier the
model has no multiplier for leaves the cost unknown.

NewAssertionLink.description: A writer resolves text hashes against its accepting read snapshot.

NewBackfillJob.description: A new backfill job, as the writer stores it.

provider.description: The web chat, by the extension's name for it.

since.description: Only conversations the provider changed at or after this time (ms).

NewChatAction.description: A new chat action, as the writer stores it.

request_key.description: The request's idempotency key: a resent request is the same action.

NewVariant.description:
A rendition submitted through the authored write path. Provenance is
computed by the accepting surface before constructing this value.

NormalizedReadSpan.description:
Resolver-produced coordinates kept in acknowledged Run custody. Source
identity is retained metadata, never a claim that all source text was read.

NoteIntent.description: Original spellings are declared provenance, never runtime reference aliases.

Notice.description: The evaluator has already applied quiet hours and the shared host budget.

budget_passive_count.description:
The evaluator supplies a cumulative count of budget-downgraded notices.
Such notices update one host summary rather than showing individually.

command_hint.description: Shown when the server cannot offer actions.

data_loss.description: Critical urgency is reserved for capture losing data now.

via.description: Desktop actions are operator acts, never acts by a rule's author.

NotificationState.description:
Persist this beside the product's delivery records. An unknown attempt is
deliberately terminal: after a crash there is no safe automatic resend.

ObjectExecutionBinding.description:
An exact object read has no semantic query or invented question identity.
Serialized fields record inputs; only a current pinned Reader derives them.

imports.description:
The original store's recorded import classifications. These are source
metadata, never observations minted at the receiving store.

intent.description: Exact semantic intent encoding covered by the original content hash.

records.description:
Exact available predecessor envelopes and alternate encodings of one
observed JSON value, separate from unavailable acquisition spelling.

request.description:
Exact retained JSON in the named source encoding. NativeProjection
identifies an SDK projection encoding, not unavailable ingress spelling.

configuration.description: Identity of the loaded deployment definition, not a rule-supplied path.

OutputBinding.description: Deferred output scopes are syntax only and must pass shared binding before execution.

unit.description: Actual row domain supplied by the product, used for nested implicit sources.

PageBudget.description:
Logical delivery caps captured before per-page response framing is reserved.
A continuation reuses all caps; an explicit override changes only that page.

Precision.description: Precision is carried separately from the represented half-open period.

Production.description:
What the harness recorded about producing a message: the settings it
ran with, who asked for it, and the API's own diagnostics. Measurement
reads these; none of it is content.

advisor_model.description: The model consulted as an advisor for this response.

api_error.description: The API error this message reports, instead of a response.

cache_miss.description:
Why the prompt cache missed, as the API reported it, with the
tokens it cost.

effort.description: Reasoning effort the request asked for (`low`, `medium`, `high`).

first_token_ms.description: Time to the first token of the response.

permission.description:
The permission decision for the tool call this message answers:
decision, its source and the kind of reason.

phase.description: Provider response channel, such as commentary or final.

quota.description:
The subscription's quota state the tool reported with this
response: which windows, how used, when they reset.

refusal.description: The refusal category and explanation, when the model refused.

request.description:
The harness's ID for the API request that produced this message,
which its request records carry.

request_id.description: The model API's own ID for the request (Anthropic `requestId`).

requested_model.description:
The model the request named, when the one that answered differs
(a fallback) or carries a variant suffix.

response_boundary_unknown.description:
These recorded items have no evidenced model-response grouping.
None is an absent update; a supplied false remains distinct.

turn_origin.description: What started the turn, when not a person at the terminal (`sdk`).

PromptKind.description:
A user prompt's category. `Harness` also marks runtime-written notices
carried under another native role; the other kinds remain user categories.
This keeps harness material out of counts of what a person or model wrote.

oneOf.description: Prose a person typed.
A slash command, shell escape or memory line.

Text the harness wrote: tool results, interruption notices, local
command output, injected reminders or assistant-shaped runtime notices.

Text another model wrote as this session's prompt: a subagent's
task, a coordinator's follow-up, a peer agent's message.

QueryExecutionOptions.description: Execution choices that remain after semantic references have been bound.

direct_reference.description: Actual accepted direct presentation, independent of semantic query identity.

ranking_identity.description: The actual provider, model and vector basis required by this execution.

QueryRun.description: One accepted execution. Authorship is computed at the daemon boundary.

QuotaReading.description:
The subscription quota a tool reported with a response, read from its
own wire format by the origin's parser.

credits.description: Prepaid credits left, as the tool wrote the number.

QuotaWindow.description: The state of one limit as the tool reported it with a response.

from_first_response.description:
The window starts with the first response after the previous one
ended, not on a fixed schedule.

limit.description: The tool's name for the limit (`codex`, `five_hour`, `seven_day`).

status.description: The tool's own word for the state (`allowed`, `rejected`).

ReadDelivery.description: Paging and streaming share selection and view; only transfer changes.

ReadDirection.description: Direction is part of the authenticated content-navigation intent.

oneOf.description: Resume at the first unconsumed character, as captured by the prior page.
Read content strictly before this page start after validating its digest.

ReadOptions.description: Absent expansions distinguish defaults from explicit unsupported options.

output_lines.description: Head and tail lines of expanded tool output. Zero keeps the complete output.

character.description: Unicode scalar position in the complete C1-safe encoded ReadItem JSON.

item_hash.description: Digest of that complete encoded item, including its original Source.

ordinal.description:
Position in the selected row's prepared metadata view, before layout.
This is independent of a message's original physical-session order.

ReadSpanBinding.description: One actual selected span source, never a native/fragment fallback on replay.

membership.description: Digest of the actual indexed stored-grain metadata, not permissions.

ReplayBinding.description: Rebinding uses these captured inputs, never current names or the wall clock.

evidence.description:
Evidence is preserved at match time. Scores never define occurrence or
change identity; the adapter supplies the complete result order.

Rule.description:
Authored fields only. Identity and authorship are supplied by the product's
write path; `deny_unknown_fields` prevents a client forging daemon metadata.

RunBinding.description:
A continuation retains one bounded reference to the original execution.
Its own envelope is provenance of this invocation, never old authority.

ServerToolUse.description: Server tools are billed separately from model tokens.

Session.description:
A session's own facts. Counts and times derived from its messages live
in the index, not here.

cwd.description:
Working directories in the order the session used them. A later
correction from the tool (Claude Code `relocated`) is appended.

mode.description:
How the harness ran the session, when not interactively (Claude
Code `bg` for a background session).

repo.description:
The repository the session worked in, as the tool names it (a
remote URL), when it records one.

tool_version.description: Version of the tool that wrote the session.

oneOf.description: A conversation or agent run the operator started.
A session another session spawned (a Claude Code subagent).
A side conversation kept inside its parent's file.

The model call that compacted another session's history (a Claude
Code `agent-acompact` file): the summarize prompt and the summary.

implicit.description: True when the unit was omitted and inherits its enclosing row scope.

SourceClaim.description:
One original source claim carried through a bundle. The receiving
archive keeps its actual local bundle input and chain separately.

total_bytes.description: A retained length claim; knowing it does not make outside bytes present.

container.description: One existing reference-text recipe, including its declared separators.

spans.description:
Requests that contributed to this coverage, not permissions or proof
that any one sender observed the whole union.

commit.description:
Sender selection/order evidence. Import computes receiving admission
from its actual source reading; it never trusts this as a local receipt.

oneOf.description:
The existing complete Message or Document value identity. A fragment
carrying this hash does not verify the complete value.

start.description:
Declared UTF-8 coordinates of the original request. For a non-byte
request, the unavailable prefix cannot be verified from a snippet.

TimeQuality.description:
Where an event time came from. Producers classify their own evidence;
quality never substitutes for precision or invents an unknown instant.

Timestamp.description:
A point in time as a source stated it. Unknown times are `None` at the
use site, never a zero or a guess.

TitleSource.description: Where a title came from, highest precedence first.

oneOf.description: The operator renamed it.
The tool generated it.
The tool's summary line.
The agent's name, for a spawned session.
The imported file's name, used when no recorded title is available.

ToolAction.description:
What a tool call does. Each origin's parser maps its own tool names to
one of these; everything after the parser reads only the action.

oneOf.description: Runs a shell command; `command` holds it.
Runs code in a sandbox (a Python cell, a code-mode script).
Searches files, symbols or tools.
Starts another agent.
A tool an MCP server provides.

ToolOutcome.description: How a tool call ended. Kinds never collapse into one success figure.

oneOf.description: The call was made and no result ever arrived.
A result exists but its status cannot be read.
Started in the background; completion has not been seen yet.

Usage.description:
Token counts for one model response or recorded usage observation, by kind: uncached input, cached
input, output and reasoning, plus cache writes. A count the source did
not report is `None`, never 0.

cache_write.description: Input tokens written to a cache, billed apart from plain input.

cache_write_1h.description:
The part of `cache_write` written with a one-hour lifetime, which is
billed at a higher rate than the default five-minute writes.

cached_input.description: Input tokens read from a cache.

input.description: Input tokens not served from a cache.

reasoning.description: Reasoning tokens, when the source reports them apart from output.

speed.description:
A generation mode priced differently from the standard one, as the
tool records it (`fast`, `standard`).

UserOutcome.description:
What a user write created, or found already created by the same
request.

id.description: The note, delivery or setting row the request wrote.

repeat.description: The request had already been written; nothing changed.

UserRequest.description: One user write with the request that carries it.

oneOf.description: A trusted daemon checkpoint with its immutable signal outbox and receipts.

prior.description: Digest of the canonical checkpoint resolved before this update.

oneOf.description: A saved query whose previous revision is resolved by name.
Context prepared for a recipient, with its exact text.
Advice already printed by a hook, recorded with its delivered outcome.
What happened to a prepared delivery.

The exact rows a query returned, kept to be read back as
`result:<id>`.

read_at.description: What the query read: its resolved time, as JSON.

rows_json.description: The stored rows, match rows and their columns, as JSON.

machine.description: `None` for an archive-wide key, otherwise this machine.

oneOf.description:
A chat action the operator queued; a resent request finds the
action it made.

The extension instance `by` takes the oldest queued chat action;
`NotFound` when none is queued or another is out.
What the instance holding a chat action's claim reports.
The operator approves or declines a held submit.

The operator starts a backfill job; the provider's job that has not
ended is found instead of a second one.

The extension instance `by` takes the job it holds or the oldest
waiting one; `NotFound` when there is none.
What the instance holding a backfill job's claim reports.
The operator stops a backfill job.

Variant.description:
One revision. Parts stream independently so a rendition of a large
session never requires a session-sized collection.

VariantEffect.description: Exact authored records carried by preparation and confirmation.
